title: Respiratory Therapy
author: Dayone Koo
_comment: PROGRAM EVALUATION (evaluate-program skill), not a role report. Subject is the PROGRAM (Foothill College x TOP 121000), not a job title. Destination SOCs are DERIVED, not authored: crosswalk(121000) = 4 SOCs, intersected with SECTORS['health'].socs and minus ALL_OTHER/PROMOTION/EXPERIENCE_5YR guards = 1 (29-1126). Dropped: 25-1071 Postsecondary Teachers, 29-2099 Health Technologists All Other, 99-9999. House rule: EVIDENCE-FORWARD, NO VERDICT — the prose states throughput, trend, destination health and peer standing and stops there; it never says 'at risk' or 'underperforming'. live_postings and competencies are reused verbatim from foothill-respiratory-therapist (same SOC, already verified against the O*NET pool and the CareerOneStop scrape). EDITION 2026-09-18: crosswalk_chain true — the TOP–CIP–SOC Crosswalk section now argues the destinations; the demand note keeps only the COE sentence.
lede: This evaluation assembles labor-market supply and demand evidence for Foothill College's Respiratory Therapy program (TOP 121000): regional demand for the occupations it leads to, its award and enrollment trends alongside other colleges offering the same program in the region, and how its courses align with the work of those occupations.
demand_note: [According to the Centers of Excellence](https://datastudio.google.com/u/0/reporting/5060057c-b9ba-4081-9ed7-83356eaa7061), Respiratory Therapists (SOC 29-1126) have roughly 210 openings a year in the Bay Area.
alignment_note: The colleges offering TOP 121000 in the Bay Area. Each supports SOC 29-1126 through the same TOP–CIP–SOC crosswalk.
award_note: Awards conferred each year by each college's program. An empty cell means DataMart reported no data.
enrollment_note: Enrollment each term in each college's program. An empty cell means DataMart reported no data.

29-1126.description: Assesses, treats, and cares for patients with breathing disorders — initiating therapeutic procedures and operating the full range of respiratory care equipment.

curriculum_note: O*NET maintains a set of detailed work activities that identify the competencies central to each job. Below, the Respiratory Therapy program's courses are mapped to the work activities of its destination occupation, based on how each course is described in its Course Outline of Record (COR).
chain_note: TOP 1210.00 maps to a single federal code and a single occupation: Respiratory Therapists.
